## Install — no GitHub CLI, no tokens, no SSH keys

Download the **Source code (zip)** below, extract, and run the bundled installer. Same flow on every OS.

**macOS / Linux**
```bash
cd jtr-0.5.3
./install.sh
```

**Windows**
```powershell
cd .\jtr-0.5.3\
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1
```

The installer fetches `uv` if needed, then runs `uv tool install` on the extracted source. See [INSTALL.md](https://github.com/BD-AI-SDLC/jtr/blob/main/INSTALL.md) for manual steps and troubleshooting.

## What's new

`jtr auth sso` no longer gives up when your saved cookies have expired — the exact case it exists to fix. If you have been reaching for `jtr auth sso --force` to get logged in, you can stop.

- **Fixed: `jtr auth sso` died instead of opening a browser.** Before launching one it probes the saved cookies to see whether a browser is needed at all. When those cookies are stale, the Bosch WebSEAL gateway answers that probe with its own HTML login page under an HTTP **200** — a shape the probe did not recognize as "logged out". So the command aborted with a wall of raw HTML (`Unexpected response: status=200 ct=text/html body='<!DOCTYPE HTML …'`) and never opened the browser. The probe is only a shortcut, so failing it now always falls through to the browser, whatever the reason.
- **Fixed: `jtr auth pat` could delete a working token.** If the gateway intercepted the verification request, the token was never actually checked by Jira — but the command read that as "token rejected" and wiped it from `.env`. It now keeps the token and tells you the gateway is the problem.
- **Causes are no longer swallowed.** A failed cookie probe prints why before the browser opens, and the SSO timeout reports the last thing it saw (`Last seen: status=… ct=… url=…`) instead of only asking whether you completed the login. This matters for the failures a browser *cannot* fix — off-VPN, dead DNS, or a base URL missing its context path — which previously ended in a five-minute wait and a misleading message.
- **Fixed: an unreadable cookie file no longer breaks the browser launch.** It is discarded and SSO starts from a clean session.
- **Docs:** `jtr auth sso --force` is no longer presented as the fix for expired cookies. Plain `jtr auth sso` handles that. `--force` now means only what it says — open a browser even though the current cookies are valid, e.g. to log in as a different user or pick up changed permissions.

## Upgrading

Nothing to do beyond installing. No config, cookie, or `.env` changes.

## Assets
- `install.sh` — macOS / Linux installer
- `install.ps1` — Windows installer
- `jtr-0.5.3-py3-none-any.whl`, `jtr-0.5.3.tar.gz` — build artifacts (auto-detected by the installers if placed alongside them)
